stories.title: Bill proposing quarterly gas pricing lands in Senate
summary: ISLAMABAD: In what is set to stir a new controversy, a bill proposing quarterly determination of natural gas prices landed in the upper House of Parliament on Friday.

The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was introduced in the House by Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry at a time when the daily fuel pricing mechanism has drawn widespread criticism.
The bill also empowers the federal government to advise Ogra to carry forward the entire or part of a quarterly adjustment to its forthcoming half-yearly determination under Section 8.

stories.title: 'I will never go back to sea': 11 fishermen released from Indian captivity reunite with families in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: 11 Pakistani fishermen, after spending several years in Indian jails for unknowingly crossing over to Indian waters while fishing, were reunited with their families in Karachi on Friday morning.

Pakistani fishermen reunite with families at Edhi Centre on October 30. — White Star/ Fahim Siddiqi Asked how his boat crossed over to the other side, he said that they experienced an engine failure, following which the boat drifted towards Indian waters.
Pakistani fishermen reunite with families at Edhi Centre on October 30. — White Star/ Fahim Siddiqi “He served his sentence two years ago, but still he has not returned home.

stories.title: Spanish transport minister refuses to resign over second major train crash on his watch
summary: Spain’s transport minister on Friday rejected calls for his resignation over the second train accident on his watch to cause mass casualties this year, as authorities worked to identify the victims from a crash that left at least 69 dead.

Authorities can’t rule out more fatalities No additional bodies were found when rescue teams overturned a train carriage on Thursday, Castilla-La Mancha regional leader Emiliano Garcia-Page said on TVE.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Friday vowed to find out what caused the accident. “It is unacceptable for a country like Spain, with such a strong high-speed rail system, to suffer two accidents of this nature and magnitude in a single year,” he said.

stories.title: Pakistan Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts in response to firing at Angoor Adda: state media
summary: It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.
Around mid-October, the state media reported that security forces had again responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in KP’s Upper Kurram.
It quoted security sources as saying that several personnel of the Afghan Taliban were “reportedly killed during the Pakistan Army’s retaliatory action along the Ghuzgarhi border”.

stories.title: PSL franchises allowed seven retentions, must release top-tier player if maximum limit exercised
summary: The provision, unanimously approved by all eight franchises at a tournament operations workshop at Gaddafi Stadium on Thursday, is among the key regulations finalised ahead of the PSL 12 player auction scheduled for January 23.
The auction, which will be only the second in PSL history, will operate under a salary cap of Rs45 crore for each franchise.

The regulations were finalised during a workshop chaired by PSL chief executive Salman Naseer, with all eight franchises reaching unanimous agreement after reviewing the auction rules clause by clause.

stories.title: FCC says not implementing SC's verdicts amounts to 'challenging the very framework of the legal system'
summary: On Friday, FCC judge, Justice Ali Baqar Najafi, emphasised that the orders of the SC, as the then-apex court before the 27th Constitutional Amendment, were “not merely recommendations or advisories but they are legal mandate that must be followed”.

Justice Najafi was a member of a three-judge bench, which was headed by FCC Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan, that had taken up a set of contempt of court petitions on the non-implementation of the SC judgement.

Reverting to the case, the FCC noted that the SC judgement required that the beneficiary employees would have to undergo relevant tests applicable to their post to be conducted by the Federal Public Service Commission (FPSC) within three months.

stories.title: Binance's $6.3bn hack: How crypto insurance works
summary: Digital asset insurance is a range of policies designed to protect cryptocurrency exchanges, custodians and other companies operating in the sector against financial losses arising from the theft of digital assets, cyberattacks, technology failures and other business risks.

Unlike traditional insurance, these policies are tailored to risks associated with blockchain technology, including the theft or loss of private keys, wallet security breaches, smart contract vulnerabilities and failures in digital asset custody.
Do traditional crime and cyber insurance policies cover crypto?

stories.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia agree to boost cooperation in oil, refineries and minerals
summary: Both sides underscored that the strong defence and strategic partnership between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia provides a foundation for broader regional peace, stability and economic cooperation.

Malik invited Saudi Arabia’s Vice Minister of Mining, Khalid al-Mudafier, to attend the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum, scheduled to be held in Islamabad on November 12 and 13, highlighting further opportunities for cooperation and investment in Pakistan’s minerals sector.
The minister assured the ambassador that Pakistan deeply valued its historic relationship with Saudi Arabia and remained committed to expanding cooperation across strategic sectors.

stories.title: In meeting with Balakrishnan, PM admires Singapore's 'remarkable economic transformation'
summary: They underscored the importance of sustained high-level exchanges and discussed ways to further enhance cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity and skills development, while promoting business-to-business exchanges and people-to-people contacts, the statement added.

Dar and Balakrishnan also discussed cooperation at multilateral fora and Pakistan’s enhanced engagement with Asean, particularly in the context of Singapore’s forthcoming chairmanship of the body in 2027.

Delegation-level talks Later, their opening remarks from delegation-level talks between the two sides were televised, with Dar saying that the depth of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and Singapore was not reflected in economic ties.

stories.title: Disrupted LPG supply
summary: THE petroleum minister’s explanation in the National Assembly that the recent closure of the Iran border has disrupted liquefied petroleum gas supplies and driven up prices identifies a major cause of the current crisis.
Further, why were no contingency measures taken before the Iran border closure, especially when the authorities knew that the onset of winter would push up demand?
Blaming the Iran border closure is but an attempt to cover up the ministry’s failure to do its basic duty: ensure adequate supplies ahead of the closure and enforce the official fuel price.

stories.title: Crypto exchange Binance freezes assets after $6.3bn 'complex' security breach
summary: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Friday it was working to resolve a “complex attack” that hit around $6.3 billion in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft.

Blockchain investigation firm TRM Labs said Thursday it had “high confidence” that the Binance hack was also orchestrated by TraderTraitor, citing “robust on and off-chain intelligence.” “Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists,” TRM said.
Crypto prices tumble For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform.

stories.title: Short-term inflation rises to 11.32pc in last week of October, driven by perishable food prices
summary: Short-term inflation has remained in double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely on the back of persistent increases in petroleum and diesel prices.
The data showed that of the 51 essential items monitored during the week, the prices of 15 commodities increased, while those of 12 items declined.
Last week, short-term inflation rose to 11.85pc year-on-year, driven largely by higher wheat flour prices, according to data released by the PBS.

stories.title: PPP delegation calls on Senate opposition leader, urges participation in proposed committee on electoral reforms
summary: Rehman added that Abbas had welcomed the PPP delegation, expressed gratitude to Bilawal and said they would respond to the proposal after consultation. “We are hopeful that their response will be positive,” she said.

A day earlier, another PPP delegation invited Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai to participate in the parliamentary committee to promote consultation and discussion among parliamentary representatives on electoral reforms.
The PPP chairman had invited the opposition to join the Parliamentary electoral reforms process and “engage with the federal government”.

stories.title: Court grants NCCIA four-day physical remand of suspect in counterfeit US postage stamp scam
summary: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Friday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) a further four-day physical remand of the prime suspect in a Rs35 billion fraud involving the online sale of counterfeit US postage stamps.
The NCCIA produced suspect Faheem Akram and his co-suspect, Naeem, before the court after their previous four-day remand expired.
The initial investigation revealed that the suspect had allegedly been operating a website since August 2023 through which he sold more than five million counterfeit US postage labels online.

stories.title: LHC directs Noreen Niazi’s counsel to file separate plea for medical treatment, family meetings
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court on Friday directed the counsel for Noreen Niazi, sister of former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan, to file a separate miscellaneous application seeking medical treatment and family meetings.

Justice Abher Gul Khan issued the direction while hearing a petition filed by Sakeena Niazi challenging the extension of the preventive detention of PTI founder Imran Khan’s two sisters, Noreen and Dr Uzma Khan.

The detention had come amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party had called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

stories.title: Six feared dead in helicopter crash in Indian Himalayan state, media report
summary: Six people ‌were feared dead in a helicopter crash in the Indian Himalayan state of ​Uttarakhand on Friday, television channels ​reported, adding that bad weather was ⁠suspected to be the cause.
The helicopter ​was flying from Badrinath, a prominent ​pilgrimage destination for Hindus located in the mountains, to Dehradun city, carrying five passengers ​and a pilot, news agency ANI ​reported.
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said his ‌office ⁠had received information about a helicopter crashing near a village in the Joshimath area.

stories.title: Pakistan seek perfect finish
summary: A gruelling battle is expected as Pakistan take on Sri Lanka in the ODI tri-series final at the Gaddafi Stadium Lahore on Saturday (today).

Pakistan, who suffered an eight-wicket defeat against Sri Lanka in their last league match, have had two successive days of training and are expected to have worked hard on addressing their weaknesses.
Pakistan's senior batsman Salman Ali Agha said the team could win the final if they played to their full potential.

stories.title: Politics casts shadow over Olympic sport
summary: IOC president Kirsty Coventry's desire is that "politics does not take over on the field of play", but Ukraine and former executives from her organisation have told AFP that politics and sport remain inseparable.

"Until that moment, isolation is not political -- it is a matter of basic human decency." Former International Olympic Committee marketing executive Terrence Burns told AFP that globally speaking, "sport has never been separate from politics".
"The boycott agenda of the eighties very nearly destroyed the Olympic movement," Michael Payne, a former IOC marketing chief, told AFP.

stories.title: Cop martyred in KP's Bajaur as terrorists attack police post: official
summary: BAJAUR: A police officer was martyred after terrorists attacked a police post in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur district, officials said on Friday.
The attack on the police post in Silai Pati area in the remote Barang tehsil, bordering Malakand district, occurred late on Thursday night.

Mansoor Khan, a spokesperson for the district police, while confirming the attack, told Dawn that a group of Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists targeted the Silai Pati police post, prompting the personnel to retaliate bravely and courageously.

stories.title: Rubio hosts G20 ministers as Iran, Ukraine wars divide members
summary: Few breakthroughs are expected this week from the Group of 20 economies -- which include China, India, Russia, Japan, Germany and France -- as officials face divisions over Moscow's war on Ukraine and fallout from conflict with Iran.

Rubio's encounter with Lavrov -- whose presence adds an additional layer of tension -- will be closely watched as Washington pursues diplomacy on Ukraine while seeking Moscow's cooperation on reining in fuel prices, a key campaign issue in the midterms.

Also read: US irks G20 ministers by bringing back Russia, barring journalists Trump has eased some sanctions on Moscow recently while touting a deal for Russia to sell diesel as prices soared, squeezing Americans.

stories.title: 'You are disgusting': Trump lashes out at reporter as he cancels weekend rallies ahead of midterm polls
summary: US President Donald Trump is scrapping two of his last midterm election rallies, his Republican Party said Thursday, as the 80-year-old leader lashed out at a reporter who asked if he was “sick of travelling”. “You’re sick to ask that question.
Instead of the events in Kansas and Iowa, Trump will hold a “large number” of virtual “telerallies” in a series of states, the Republican National Committee said.

MAGA Inc, a campaign funding group aligned with Trump, said on Thursday it would host a series of “tele-rallies” with the president in at least 19 states, including Kansas and Iowa, before Election Day.

stories.title: The Exhibition in the Library: Agatha Christie display shines light on famed writer
summary: A new London exhibition shines a spotlight on crime novelist Agatha Christie, looking at how her life, interests and travels inspired her hugely successful whodunnits.
"Most people who know about Agatha Christie — and to be fair, most people do know about Agatha Christie — think of the work.
But I think what this gives you is an insight into the woman behind the work," James Prichard, Christie's great-grandson and CEO of Agatha Christie Limited, said.

stories.title: Russell Brand found monogamy 'difficult', wife tells UK rape trial
summary: The wife of British comedian and actor Russell Brand testified on Thursday at his trial for rape and sexual assault, saying he had found monogamy "difficult" but became an "amazing" husband.
Gallacher and Brand married in 2017 and have three children.
Four of the charges relate to years before Brand met Gallacher.

stories.title: Fire destroys 35 shops at furniture market in Karachi
summary: A fire that broke out at a furniture market near Kamran Chowrangi in Karachi’s Gulistan-e-Jauhar was brought under control after a firefighting operation, destroying around 35 shops and 10 to 12 shanties, along with the goods stored inside them.
The fire also spread to an adjacent residential building, but firefighters brought the blaze under control there before it caused further damage.

The Sindh Building Control Ordinance gave the authority powers to take corrective action against dangerous buildings, while Gul Plaza's incomplete records and ineffective fire-safety oversight also reflected institutional failure.

stories.title: Asim Azhar celebrates 30th birthday with new song
summary: Singer Asim Azhar marked his 30th birthday by releasing his latest song, Ajnabi, as a gift to his fans.

Out nowwwww." View this post on Instagram Just hours before Azhar's birthday post, Aamir had shared an Instagram story showing herself riding scooters around a neighbourhood with a male companion, while the singer's new song played in the background.
With the release of Ajnabi, heartfelt family moments and Aamir's appearance in his birthday album, Azhar's milestone celebration gave fans plenty to talk about.

stories.title: Critics doubt Nehr-i-Khayyam’s EIA plan as construction continues in Karachi
summary: The opponents of the project questioned the government’s decision to approach Sepa at this stage, arguing that the move raises more questions than it answers about the project’s planning, environmental impact and the authorities’ handling of the construction.
Sepa sources said it was “almost impossible” to conduct an environmental review or EIA of the project while construction work was already underway.

Opposing any commercial activity along Nehr-i-Khayyam, he warned that narrowing or closing the natural waterway could affect the city’s rainwater drainage system and deman­ded that the Sindh government make the project’s PC-I, EIA report and other relevant documents public.

stories.title: ATC judge, who denied Hammad Azhar’s remand, made officer on special duty
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) has made District & Sessions Judge (D&SJ) Sardar Muhammad Akram Khan, the administrative judge of the antiterrorism court (ATC), an officer on special duty (OSD).

On Tuesday last, the judge had heard the case of the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) leader Hammad Azhar, who was presented before his court with a request to extend his physical remand in the Jinnah House attack case related to May 9 riots.
Before his posting to Lahore ATC, D&SJ Akram was serving as banking court judge in Sialkot.

stories.title: Container truck gets stuck under flyover pier in Charsadda
summary: Motorists have urged the relevant authorities and project engineers to inspect the site and determine why the vehicle could not pass beneath the structure.

Concerns raised over project’s design They also called for a technical investigation to establish whether the incident resulted from a design flaw, differences in road and bridge levels, or the movement of an oversized vehicle.

The relevant authorities have been urged to investigate the incident, verify the approved design and take appropriate corrective measures to ensure the safe passage of vehicles and uninterrupted traffic flow on Mardan Road.

stories.title: PHC again seeks govt response over health facilities in South Waziristan
summary: It again issued notices to the respondents, including the chief secretary, health secretary and director general (health services), directing them to file comments in the petition filed by several residents of Upper South Waziristan.

Issues notices to chief, health secretaries and DG (health services) They requested the court to declare that the denial of adequate health facilities to people in Upper South Waziristan district was unconstitutional and a violation of their fundamental rights.

He added that upon the creation of Upper South Waziristan district, the respondents became legally and constitutionally bound to provide essential infrastructure, including administrative offices, law-enforcement system and most importantly a fully functional DHQ hospital.

stories.title: LHC asks Noreen Niazi's counsel to file separate plea for medical care, family access
summary: PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja also appeared before the court and raised concerns over Noreen's medical condition.
Raja calls Noreen's detention unjustified Raja criticised the continued detention of Imran's three sisters, saying there was no justification for keeping Noreen in custody despite her illness.

Noreen was healthy before detention, says husband Noreen's husband, Ahad Khan, said she had been completely healthy before being sent to jail and said that her health had deteriorated during detention. “Before going to jail, Noreen had no health problems.

stories.title: Retired schoolteacher shot dead in Lower Dir's Talash area
summary: LOWER DIR: A retired schoolteacher was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in Bagh Dushkhel village in Talash area on Wednesday evening, prompting his family to give police 72 hours to arrest the suspects.

The family appealed to the Lower Dir district police officer (DPO), the Malakand deputy inspector general of police (DIG) and the provincial government to ensure immediate arrest of the suspects involved in Shireen’s murder and bring them to justice.
Meanwhile, Talash police claimed to have arrested a suspect, Waris Khan, son of Syed Ahmad Khan, along with the alleged murder weapon within two hours of the killing in Bagh Dushkhel.

stories.title: Public Accounts Committee orders inquiry into faulty diagnostic machines at KMC hospitals
summary: KARACHI: The Public Accou­nts Committee (PAC) of the Sindh Assembly was informed on Thursday that X-ray, ultrasound, ECG and other essential diagnostic machines had remained non-functional for years in several Karachi Metropolitan Corpor­ation (KMC) run hospitals.

Audit officials told the PAC that during the inspection, diagnostic equipment, including X-ray, ultrasound and ECG mach­ines, was found to be non-functional in Sobhraj Maternity Hos­p­ital and other KMC-run facilities.

Mr Khuhro directed the CMIT to conduct a comprehensive inqu­iry into the non-functional X-ray, CT scan, ultrasound, MRI and ECG machines in all hospitals under the KMC, as well as other hospitals across Sindh, and submit a report within one month.

stories.title: Two civilians hurt in quadcopter attack in Upper South Waziristan
summary: SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: Two civilians were injured in an alleged quadcopter attack in Barwand area of Servekai tehsil, Upper South Waziristan, on Thursday, local sources and police said.
According to local sources, an unidentified quadcopter targeted a populated area in Barwand, leaving two civilians, Saud Mehsud and Mir Azam Khan Mehsud, injured.
The residents said quadcopter flights and attacks in the area had continued, causing fear and concern among local population.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court stays repatriation of employees serving on deputation
summary: Justice Raja Inaam Ameen Minhas issued the directions while hearing a petition filed by Khalid Mahmood and others, challenging the proposed repatriation of employees who, according to their counsel, have been serving in the departments concerned for more than 15 years.
The counsel argued that the proposed repatriation notification was discriminatory, unjustified and an abuse of authority.
They contended that the employees had served in their respective departments for over 15 years and had, as a result, acquired a legal right to permanent status.

stories.title: Excavation for housing scheme in Islamabad's Kurri endangers school building
summary: According to a letter issued by the FDE, large amounts of earth and soil have been continuously excavated from three sides of the school building, leaving the structure exposed and vulnerable at the edge of a steep vertical drop.

FDE says large amounts of soil have been excavated from three sides of girls school building The FGEHA project is called Margalla Orchard Scheme, while the CDA project, Margalla Enclave, is a joint venture between the CDA and the Defence Housing Authority (DHA).

Crucially, vast amounts of earth and soil have been continuously excavated from three sides of the school building, leaving the structure severely heightened, exposed and entirely compromised at the edge of a steep vertical drop,” the FDE letter addressed to the FGEHA stated.

stories.title: China-gifted hospital inaugurated in Chak Shahzad after remaining unused for years
summary: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday inaugurated the 250-bed Pak-China Friendship Hospital at Chak Shahzad, gifted by China, that had remained unused since the Covid-19 epidemic in 2020.
Speaking on the occasion, the prime minister announced that the hospital, to be run by Indus, a private organisation, will provide free medical treatment to patients.

I rejected it and thought that the hospital should be named as Pak-China Friendship Hospital,” the prime minister said. “The hospital will cater to patients not only from Islamabad but other nearby region,” he added.

stories.title: PSX gains over 1,130 points despite early-session volatility
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange traded in positive territory in midday dealing on Friday, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index up 1,136.74 points, or 0.69%, at 166,873.49.
The index had closed the previous session at 165,736.75.
Read: PSX extends recovery for fourth session The current reading keeps the index comfortably above the prior close, with the bulk of the day’s range still intact.

stories.title: Security forces foil drone attack attempt in Balochistan's Kharan district: state media
summary: Security forces foiled an attempt by Fitna al-Hindustan to carry out a drone attack in Balochistan, Radio Pakistan reported on Friday, citing security sources.
According to sources, terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan attempted to target a checkpost in the Albat area of Kharan district using low-grade drones.

Over the past few years, Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist attacks, with militants frequently targeting convoys, abducting security personnel and civilians, and attacking security and civilian installations.
